summary.title: NHS Scotland vs NHS England: who does better?
summary.answer: Neither, overall. It depends which door you walk through.
summary.bottom_line: Scotland is better at getting you seen. England is better at getting you treated.

summary.twist: Scotland spends 36% more per person on adult social care ({{social_care_spend.scotland}} vs {{social_care_spend.england}}), yet has roughly twice as many delayed hospital discharges per person.

myths.myth: One NHS is clearly outperforming the other.
myths.lead: Scotland leads on getting seen. England leads on getting treated. On cancer waits and public satisfaction they are level, and both fall short of every core standard.

card.label: England's hospital activity. Scotland is below

points: Scotland has {{gp_per_100k.scotland}} GPs per 100,000 people against {{gp_per_100k.england}} in England, and prescriptions are free.
England has recovered planned hospital activity to above pre-pandemic levels. Scotland has not.
Neither country meets the 95% four-hour A&E standard or its waiting time standards.
myths.meaning: Ask “better at what?” If you need a GP or a prescription, Scotland does better. If you need a hip replacement, England has recovered faster.
myths.caveat: Several measures are defined differently in each country. Where that matters, the figures are flagged.

myths.myth: Scotland only does better on GPs and A&E because it gets far more NHS money.
myths.verdict_detail: The funding gap has nearly gone
myths.lead: Scotland spent 22% more per person on health than England at devolution. By 2024/25 the gap was {{health_spend_premium.scotland}}: {{health_spend_per_head.scotland}} against {{health_spend_per_head.england}}.

card.label: Scotland's extra health spend per person, 1999/2000
Scotland's extra health spend per person, 2024/25
extra adult social care spend per person

points: England's health budget grew faster. Scotland chose to put relatively more into social care and other services.
Total public service spending is 22% higher per person in Scotland, so the extra money exists. It mostly isn't going to the NHS.
Figures are cash per person. Scotland's older, sicker and more rural population means 2% more likely buys less care per patient.
myths.meaning: Scotland's edge on GPs and A&E can't be put down to a big NHS funding advantage. That advantage has mostly gone.
myths.caveat: The IFS warns Scotland's 2026/27 health budget grows very slowly. Audit Scotland judged NHS Scotland not financially sustainable in December 2025.

myths.myth: Scotland's lower life expectancy proves NHS Scotland gives worse care.
myths.lead: Scotland's life expectancy is about two years behind England's, but only about half a year behind North East England, a region with similar deprivation and industrial history.

card.label: life expectancy gap to all of England
gap between Scotland's most and least deprived areas (men)

points: Men in Scotland live {{life_exp_m.scotland}} years on average, against {{life_exp_m.north_east}} in North East England and {{life_exp_m.england}} across England.
The bigger gap is inside Scotland: {{deprivation_gap_m.scotland}} between men in the most and least deprived areas.
Once someone is a cancer patient, treatment times are near identical: {{cancer_62.scotland}} vs {{cancer_62.england}} within 62 days.
myths.meaning: Life expectancy mostly tells you about poverty, housing and history. It says little about how good the NHS is.
myths.caveat: North East England is smaller and more urban, with none of Scotland's remote and island areas.

myths.myth: Higher poverty and poor health make Scotland's long waiting lists unavoidable.
myths.lead: North East England has similar deprivation to Scotland, yet its hospitals are among the fastest in England. And Scotland's own long waits have fallen sharply in 2026.

card.label: North East and North Cumbria patients waiting under 18 weeks

points: North East and Yorkshire has been England's best-performing region on 18-week waits, ahead of wealthier regions.
Scotland's waits over 52 weeks fell from 85,856 in September 2025 to {{long_waits.scotland}} in May 2026.
About {{ttg_12wk.scotland}} of Scottish operations happen within the 12-week guarantee, and progress slowed by mid-2026.
myths.meaning: Deprivation makes the job harder, but it doesn't fix waiting times in place. Capacity, organisation and focus matter on both sides of the border.
myths.caveat: England measures the whole journey from referral to treatment. Scotland counts each stage separately. The ONS says waiting times can't be reliably compared across UK nations.

myths.myth: Scotland has more hospital staff, so it must be treating more patients.
myths.lead: Between 2019 and late 2025, NHS Scotland's hospital workforce grew by {{staff_vs_2019.scotland}}. Planned admissions fell by 4% and outpatient appointments by 5%.
points: England and Wales have restored hospital activity to above pre-pandemic levels. Scotland is the outlier, says the IFS.
Audit Scotland found performance has not improved in line with the extra money and staff.
England's productivity has risen too, but its waiting list barely moved between March 2024 and March 2025.
myths.meaning: Scotland's planned care problem is not just money or headcount. It's getting more patients through the system with the staff it already has.
myths.caveat: Productivity is hard to measure, and new staff include roles that don't show up as admissions.

myths.myth: Scotland spends 36% more on adult social care, so it has less bed blocking.
myths.lead: Scotland spends {{social_care_spend.scotland}} per person on adult social care against {{social_care_spend.england}} in England. Yet it has about {{delayed_per_100k.scotland}} delayed discharges per 100,000 people, against about {{delayed_per_100k.england}}.

card.label: adult social care spend per person
towards personal care in a Scottish care home

points: Free personal care covers care at home in full. In a care home it pays {{fpc_care_home.scotland}} towards personal care; accommodation is still means-tested.
{{complex_delays.scotland}} of Scotland's delays are complex cases, many waiting on Adults with Incapacity guardianship.
Plans for a National Care Service were dropped in 2025. The smaller Care Reform (Scotland) Act 2025 made no structural change.
myths.meaning: Scotland's extra social care money buys fairness, mostly through free care at home. It hasn't bought faster hospital discharges.
myths.caveat: Scotland uses a monthly census and bed days; England uses daily hospital returns. The per-person gap is indicative.
